newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold ends flat to firmer, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold ends flat to firmer, others mixed.

text.p: TOCOM yen-based gold futures ended flat to slightly firmer on Friday in dull trade while the other precious metals ended mixed.

Gold bullion edged higher, supported at $380 an ounce by modest physical demand from Hong Kong, Japanese traders said. Light professional buying from New York, thought to be short covering, was also noted in early Asian trading hours.

TOCOM most-active August 1997 gold settled unchanged at 1,348 yen per gram, traded narrowly from 1,347 to 1,350, after hitting a life-of-contract high of 1,352 on Thursday as the yen continued its recent slide against the dollar.
The yen/dollar rate held mostly steady today, however, lending little direction to precious metal futures.
The other months ended flat to three yen firmer, with December, at 1,365 yen, retaining its premium to the deferreds.
Gold bullion closed in Tokyo at $380.40/70 an ounce, marginally above the New York closing quote around $380.10.
Traders noted stiff resistance looming above $381, with a breach of that level likely to spur short-covering by U.S. funds that had gone massively short during gold's recent slide.
Bullion hit an 18-month low on Tuesday, with bids noted as low as $376.90, but $377 was now seen as near-term support.

Traders said the market will be monitoring the financial markets' reaction to the release later today at 1230 GMT of key U.S. September employment data. Analysts' average forecast called for a rise in non-farm payrolls of 166,000.
In the other precious metals, most-active August 1997 platinum ended one yen firmer at 1,369 yen per gram, while August 1997 palladium was off three yen at 432 yen per gram.
August 1997 silver ended 0.1 yen higher at 178.7 yen per 10 grams while the other months were 0.2 to 1.2 yen lower.
